mbti.mbtiTestIntro:
No more complicated MBTI tests!
Extroverted? Introverted?
Realistic? Idealistic?
Logical? Emotional?
Planned? Spontaneous?
Which of the 16 personality types do you belong to?
Try it with friends, lovers, and family!
It's the first step to understanding each other's personalities.
In just 1 minute, discover your MBTI tendencies
and core personality traits!
mbti.stressTestIntro:
Explode? Endure? Avoid? Discover your stress coping style!
Sudden work demands from your boss,
Unexpected conflicts with friends,
Unforeseen problem situations...
Some people explode immediately,
Some people suppress their feelings,
Some people avoid the problem.
How do you react to stress?
Looking for healthier coping strategies?
In just 3 minutes, discover your stress response pattern
and better coping methods!
mbti.datingTestIntro:
Perfect plan? Spontaneous adventure? Or comfortable at home?

Someone who books restaurants a week in advance,
Someone who moves spontaneously asking "What should we do today?",
Someone who seeks comfort saying "Watch movies at home?"

What is your dating style?
Discover your true dating style with 12 questions,
and check compatibility with your partner!

Only 3 minutes! Try it with friends and lovers 😊
mbti.signalTestIntro:
Can you tell without saying 'I love you'?

"Had a tough day?" - Is it just a question or a signal of comfort?
Why is the message reply late? Busy? Angry?
What does it mean when they suddenly hold your hand?

How well are you catching your lover's signals?
Test your signal detection ability with 12 situations!

Just 3 minutes! Try it with your lover 💕

leaderShare.title: Sharing the test link in the group chat (relay · steps)
leaderShare.body:
To see the full team analysis (grade, role mix, synergy) clearly, use a relay: after each person finishes, post the fresh link from the result screen in the chat and pass it to the next person. That one-by-one handoff is the clearest way.

① On the start screen, under “Share with friends,” copy this test page URL and post it in the group chat.

② Each teammate opens the link, finishes all 12 questions, and sees their own team-role type result.

③ On the result screen, tap “Copy team link” at the bottom. That copies a new URL with everyone who has taken the test so far baked into the address. Post that link again in the chat or send it to teammates who have not done it yet. (Repeat step ③ after each person finishes to keep the chain going.)

④ After everyone has joined, open the last shared link and on the result screen read “Our team work chemistry analysis” (role mix, synergy, missing-role warnings, etc.).

※ For the full team analysis you must relay the link through step ③. If you only want your personal result, stopping after step ② is enough.

Doing this before a meeting makes it easier to align on roles.
leaderShare.shareHint: The first link has no team data yet. Like a relay—after each person finishes, post the updated URL from “Copy team link” on the result screen so everyone’s roles are reflected in the analysis.

visionary_executor.title: ✨ Dream combo unlocked
visionary_executor.body:
You have both someone who sets direction and someone who executes.

This team structure is close to “set a goal and actually ship it.”

Note: as execution speeds up, detailed verification can slip—an Analyst role makes this combo even stronger.

coordinator_analyst.title: ✨ Balance combo unlocked
coordinator_analyst.body:
Head and heart are balanced. Decisions are less likely to swing to one extreme, and conclusions are easier for everyone to accept.

Teams with this pairing often bounce back faster after conflict.

creator_executor.title: ✨ Idea-to-ship combo unlocked
creator_executor.body:
Idea people and builders are on the same team.

While others are still debating, you may already be prototyping.

visionary.title: ⚠️ No clear direction
visionary.body: No one is naturally setting direction. The team may be running hard without a shared “where we’re going.”
visionary.prescription: Before meetings, align on “what this project must achieve” in one short sentence everyone agrees on.

executor.title: ⚠️ Weak execution engine
executor.body: There may be ideas and direction, but not enough drive to turn them into concrete output.
executor.prescription: End every meeting with explicit “who does what by when”—make it a team habit.

analyst.title: ⚠️ Weaker risk detection
analyst.body: The team moves fast, but fewer people naturally spot gaps and risks.
analyst.prescription: Rotate a “devil’s advocate” before big decisions—finding counterarguments alone cuts a lot of risk.

coordinator.title: ⚠️ Harder conflict recovery
coordinator.body: When friction appears, there may be no natural mediator.
coordinator.prescription: Watch for awkward silence in meetings. A quick “anyone see this differently?” routine helps.

creator.title: ⚠️ Few creative breakthroughs
creator.body: When stuck, radically new angles may not surface easily.
creator.prescription: Try a monthly “wildest idea” round—judgment-free brainstorming trains creative muscle.

supporter.title: ⚠️ Burnout risk
supporter.body: The team may chase results while under-supporting emotional energy.
supporter.prescription: Add a weekly check-in: “energy level 1–10 this week?”

six_roles.title: Chemistry A+ — well-rounded team 🏆
six_roles.body: All six role types show up. Strengths can cover blind spots—great synergy potential.
six_roles.caution: Swap roles occasionally so no one gets stuck in one lane—flexibility helps the whole team.

five_roles.title: Chemistry A — one role gap
five_roles.body: Roles are fairly mixed. Consciously filling the missing type can lift team chemistry a notch.

four_roles.title: Chemistry B+ — two role gaps
four_roles.body: Roles are fairly mixed. Consciously filling missing types can lift team chemistry a notch.

three_balance.title: Chemistry B — balance needed ⚖️
three_balance.body: Roles are skewed. Things may work now, but certain situations will expose weak spots.
three_balance.caution: Name missing roles in meetings: “We don’t have an Analyst—who can play that part this time?”

two_roles.title: Chemistry C — revisit structure
two_roles.body: Low role diversity. Alternate meeting items like “gap check” and “emotion check.”

one_cluster.title: Chemistry D — needs a reset 🚨
one_cluster.body: Everyone clusters in similar roles. Thinking the same way creates blind spots.
one_cluster.caution: Bring outside perspectives regularly to shrink blind spots.
